Rashi on Shabbat 51a:10:1.hebrew: אין טומנין את החמין משחשיכה ואפילו בדבר שאינו מוסיף הבל - וכדאמרן: שמא ימצא קדרתו צוננת כשירצה להטמינה, וירתיחנה בשבת. אבל אם בא להוסיף כיסוי על כיסוי משחשיכה — מוסיף:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:10:1.english: One may not insulate hot food after nightfall, and even in something that does not add heat - And [this is] as we said: Lest he find his pot cold when he wishes to insulate it, and boil it on Shabbat. But if he comes to add covering upon covering after nightfall — he may add.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:10:2.hebrew: גלופקרא - קו"ט, ויש בו הבל יותר מן הסדינין. ונוטל את הגלופקרא בימות החמה, אם ירא שמא יקדיח תבשילו מחמת רוב כיסוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:10:2.english: Gelofekara - [Old French: cot, a heavy garment]; and it retains more heat than the sheets. And he removes the gelofekara in the summer if he fears that his cooked food might burn due to excessive covering.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:11:1.hebrew: וכן היה רשב"ג - מיקל קולא אחריתי בהטמנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:11:1.english: And likewise, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel - He was lenient with another leniency regarding insulation.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:11:2.hebrew: לא אסרו - להטמין משחשיכה אלא במיחם שהוחמו בו, דהתם הוא דאיכא למיגזר שמא ירתיח. "אבל מפנה הוא ממיחם למיחם אחר ומטמין" — זהו לשון התוספתא. והיינו נמי "פינהו ממיחם למיחם מותר", דהשתא ליכא למיגזר שמא ירתיח; דהשתא אקורי קא מיקר להו במתכוין — ארתוחי מרתח להו?! בתמיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:11:2.english: They did not prohibit - insulating after nightfall except in the urn in which [the water] was heated, for it is there that there is [cause] to decree lest he heat [it]. "However, one may empty [it] from an urn into another urn and insulate" — this is the wording of the Tosefta. And this is also [the meaning of]: "If he emptied it from an urn into an urn, it is permitted," for now there is no [cause] to decree lest he heat [it]; for now he intentionally cools it — would he heat it?! [This is asked] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:12:1.hebrew: טמן - הקדרה בדבר הניטל, מה שנתן סביבותיה הוי דבר מוכן:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:12:1.english: He insulated - The pot with something that may be moved: that which he placed around it is a prepared item.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:12:2.hebrew: וכיסה - על פיה נמי דבר המוכן, כגון כלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:12:2.english: And covered [it] - Over its opening as well, [he placed] a prepared object, such as a vessel:

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:12:3.english: Or if he insulated [it] with something that may not be moved - And covered [it] with something that may be moved.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:12:4.hebrew: הרי זה נוטל ומחזיר - דהואיל והכיסוי ניטל, מגלה הקדרה ואוחזה. אבל טמן וכיסה בדבר שאינו ניטל, או אפי' טמן בדבר הניטל וכיסה בדבר שאינו ניטל — אם אין מקצת פיה מגולה, לא יטול, דאין לו במה יאחזנה. ואם תאמר: יפנה סביבותיה, הואיל ודבר הניטל הוא, ויאחזנה בדופניה, ויטנה על צדה ויפול הכיסוי, כי ההיא דתנן לקמן (פרק נוטל דף קמב:): האבן שעל פי החבית — מטה על צדה והיא נופלת, ואם היתה בין החביות — מגביהה ומטה על צדה והיא נופלת? הא אוקימנא התם בשכח, אבל במניח — נעשה בסיס לדבר האסור. והיכא דמגולה מקצתו, אין זה טלטול, שמצדדו והכיסוי נופל מאליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:12:4.english: He may take and return - For since the cover may be moved, he uncovers the pot and grasps it. But [if] he insulated and covered [it] with something that may not be moved, or even [if] he insulated with something that may be moved and covered with something that may not be moved — if part of its opening is not exposed, he may not take [it], as he has nothing by which to grasp it. And if you say: Let him clear away [the material] around it, since it is something that may be moved, and grasp [the pot] by its sides, and tilt it on its side so that the cover falls off, like that which we learned later (chapter Notel, daf 142b): "A stone that is on the mouth of a barrel — one tilts [the barrel] on its side and it falls off; and if it was between [other] barrels, he lifts it up and tilts it on its side and it falls off"? Behold, we established there [that this applies only] when one forgot [it there]; but when one placed [it intentionally], it becomes a base for a forbidden item. And where part of its [opening] is exposed, this is not [forbidden] moving, since he tilts it and the cover falls off on its own.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:1:1.english: Not due to diverse kinds - For this is not planting.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:1:2.hebrew: ולא משום מעשר - דנימא בטלה לה אגב קרקע, והרי הוא כלוקטה מתחלה, ויהא צריך לעשר על הנוסף, שמא ניתוסף:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:1:2.english: Nor due to tithes - That we might say [that] it becomes nullified to the ground, and he is like one who harvests it anew, and he would [therefore] need to tithe on the addition, lest it grew further.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:1:3.hebrew: וניטלין בשבת - שאוחזה במקצת עליה המגולין, ולא חייש אם העפר ניזוז מאליו. וה"ה לסליקוסתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:1:3.english: And they may be taken on Shabbat - For one grasps it by some of its exposed leaves, and is not concerned if the earth moves on its own; and the same applies to the selikosta [fragrant branch].

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:2:1.hebrew: לא יכסנו משתחשך - הא פרישנא טעמא בפ"ב (דף לד.): מפני מה אמרו אין טומנין בדבר שאינו מוסיף הבל משחשיכה — גזירה שמא ירתיח:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:2:1.english: He may not cover it after dark - We already explained the reason in the second chapter (daf 34a): Why did they say [that] one may not insulate in something that does not add heat once it is dark? [It is] a decree lest one boil [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:2:2.english: One may fill a jug - With cold [water].

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:2:3.hebrew: ונותן לתוך הכר - שלא יחמו בחום הקיץ והחמה, כגון כר וכסת של לבדין שאינו מחמם:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:2:3.english: And places [it] inside the pillow - So that [the water] does not become warm in the heat of the summer and the sun, such as a pillow or cushion of felt, which does not warm [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:3:1.hebrew: מותר להטמין את הצונן - מפני החמה, שלא יחמו. ולא גזרינן אטו הטמנה כדי שיחמו:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:3:1.english: It is permitted to insulate cold [food] - From the heat, so that it does not become warm; and we do not issue a decree [prohibiting this] on account of insulation [done] so that it will become warm.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:4:1.hebrew: אי ממתני' הוה אמינא הני מילי - כגון מים צוננין, שאין דרכן להטמין תחת כר וכסת לחממן, שאין מתחממין בכך. הלכך, ליכא למיגזר:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:4:1.english: If from the Mishnah, I would have said that this applies only - Such as to cold water, which it is not customary to insulate beneath a pillow or a cushion to heat it, as it does not become warm through that; therefore, there is no [reason] to issue a decree:

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:4:2.hebrew: אבל דבר שדרכו להטמין - לחמם, כגון תבשיל — אימא: לא יטמיננו מפני החמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:4:2.english: However, something that is commonly insulated - To warm [it], such as a cooked dish — I would say: he may not insulate it [even] against the heat [of the sun].

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:5:1.english: Permitted insulating cold [food] - To protect it from the heat.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:6:1.english: Filled the place of his fathers - [He was] as great as his father.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:6:2.hebrew: היה כפוף ויושב לפני רבי - מפני כבוד הנשיאות, ולא היה מורה לפניו, אע"פ שגדול הימנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:6:2.english: He would have been subordinate and sitting before Rabbi - Out of respect for the Patriarchate, and he would not have issued rulings in his presence, even though he was greater than him.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:6:3.english: The Elder has already ruled - [Rabbi] exalted him and elevated him above himself.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:7:1.english: Insulate cold [food] for me - On Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:7:2.hebrew: ואייתי לי מיא דאחים קפילא ארמאה - שהחמן נחתום נכרי, ובחול, ולאשמועינן דאין בהן משום בשולי נכרים:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:7:2.english: And bring me water that a gentile cook heated - That a gentile baker heated them, and on a weekday; and [this was stated] to teach us that they are not subject to [the prohibition of] food cooked by gentiles.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:7:3.english: In accordance with his teachers - In accordance with his teachers.

Rashi on Shabbat 51a:9:1.hebrew: אדם חשוב שאני - שהרואה אותו שהוא מיקל, עומד ומיקל יותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 51a:9:1.english: An important person is different - For one who sees him being lenient will go and be even more lenient.

Tosafot on Shabbat 51a:10:1.hebrew: כיצד הוא עושה רשב"ג אומר נוטל את הסדינין כו' - נראה לר"י ולה"ר פור"ת דל"ג "כיצד הוא עושה", דרשב"ג פליג את"ק, דלא שרי אלא להוסיף, אבל להחליף — אסור; ורשב"ג שרי אף להחליף, וכ"ש ליטול ולהחזיר אותו דבר, דלא הוי כל כך תחלת הטמנה. והיינו דקאמר: "וכן היה רשב"ג אומר", כלומר: שהיה מיקל קולא אחריתי גבי הטמנה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 51a:10:1.english: "How does he do [it]? Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: He takes the sheets, etc." - It appears to the Ri and to the Rav, Rabbi Porat, that we do not read "How does he do [it]?", for Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagrees with the first tanna, who permits only adding [to the insulation], but replacing [it] is forbidden, whereas Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permits even replacing [it] — and all the more so removing and returning that same item, as that is not so much an initial insulation. And that is why [the Tosefta] says: "And so did Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel say," meaning that he was lenient with another leniency regarding insulation.

Tosafot on Shabbat 51a:11:1.hebrew: אבל פינה ממיחם למיחם מותר - ול"ד לההוא דכירה, דבעי בפרק כירה (לעיל שבת לח:): "פינה ממיחם למיחם, מהו?" — דהתם רוצה בחמימותן, לכך יש לאסור כשהוא צונן; אבל הכא גבי הטמנה, כל כמה שהוא צונן, טפי שפיר דמי, כדאמר לעיל: "רבי התיר להטמין את הצונן". וא"ת: ורבי לא ידע לעיל דמותר להטמין את הצונן? וכי לא ידע דשמיע ליה מאבוה הכא דשרי? וי"ל: דהכא דוקא, דמוכח מילתא שנתכוין לצנן, שפינהו ממיחם למיחם; אבל קיתון של מים, דלא מוכח מידי — יהא אסור להטמין. מתוספות רבינו יהודה (ת"י):
Tosafot on Shabbat 51a:11:1.english: "However, if one emptied [the water] from an urn into an urn, it is permitted" - And [this] is not comparable to that [case] of the stove, where [the Gemara] inquires in the chapter [entitled] Kira (above, Shabbat 38b): "If one emptied [water] from an urn into an urn, what is [the ruling]?" For there, he desires its heat; therefore, there is reason to prohibit [it] when it is cold. However, here with regard to insulation, as much as it is colder, all the better, as [the Gemara] said above: "Rabbi permitted insulating cold [items]." And if you say: Did Rabbi not know above that it is permitted to insulate cold [items]? Did he not know, when he heard [it] from his father here, that it is permitted? And one can say: Here [it is permitted] specifically because the matter is evident that he intended to cool [it down], as he emptied it from an urn into an urn; but [in the case of] a jug of water, where nothing is evident, it should be prohibited to insulate. [From the Tosafot of Rabbeinu Yehudah (T"Y).]

Tosafot on Shabbat 51a:13:1.hebrew: או שטמן בדבר הניטל וכיסה בדבר שאינו ניטל - הקשה בקונט': יפנה סביבה, ויאחזנה בדופניה, ויגביהנה, ויטנה על צדה — כדתנן בפרק נוטל (לקמן שבת קמב:): "היתה בין החביות מגביהה כו'". ומתרץ: דהא אוקמינן התם בשכח, אבל במניח נעשה בסיס לדבר האסור. וקשה: דאי חשיב הכא כמניח, אם כן במגולה מקצתה היאך נוטל ומחזיר? מה בין זה לאבן שעל פי החבית, דאסרי' במניח אפי' להטותה על צדה?! ועוד קשה לר"ת: דהא תנן: "נוער את הכיסוי והן נופלות", אפי' אינן מגולות מקצתן! ועל כן אומר ר"ת: דלא חשיב כמניח, כיון שדעתו ליטלו בשבת. ובפ' נוטל (שבת דף קמג.) נתנן: "בית שמאי אומרים מגביהין מעל גבי השלחן עצמות וקליפים, וב"ה אומרים מסלק את הטבלא ומנערה", ולא חשיב לב"ה כמניח. והכא מיירי בכיסוי כעין כלי חרס שנותנים על הקדרה, שהקדרה בלועה בתוכה, ואי אפשר לנער הכיסוי אלא אם כן יגביהו קצת. ור"י מפרש: כגון שטמן הקדרה בקופה בדבר הניטל, ולמעלה מן הקדרה מילא כל הקופה בדבר שאינו ניטל, שאי אפשר לו להגיע לקדרה אם לא יטלטל דבר שאינו ניטל בידים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 51a:13:1.english: "Or if he insulated [it] in something that may be moved and covered [it] with something that may not be moved" - The Kuntres asked: Let him clear [the insulating material] around it, grasp it by its sides, lift it up, and tilt it onto its side, as we learned in a Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Notel (below, Shabbat 142b): "[If a barrel with a stone on top] was between [other] barrels, he lifts it up etc. [and tilts it on its side, and it falls]"! And he answers: For we established there [that it is permitted only] in a case where one forgot [the stone there], but if he intentionally placed [it there], it becomes a base for a forbidden item (basis ledavar ha'asur). And this is difficult: For if here it is considered an intentional placement, if so, when it is partially exposed, how may he remove and return [it]? What is the difference between this and a stone that is upon the mouth of the barrel, where we prohibit [moving it] in a case of intentional placement even to tilt it onto its side?! And furthermore, it is difficult to Rabbeinu Tam: For didn't we learn in a Mishnah: "He shakes the cover and they fall," even if they are not partially exposed?! Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam says that it is not considered an intentional placement [to make it a basis], since his intention was to remove it on Shabbat. And in the chapter [entitled] Notel (Shabbat 143a) we learned: "Beit Shammai say: One may remove bones and shells from the table; and Beit Hillel say: One removes the table board and shakes it," and according to Beit Hillel it is not considered an intentional placement [that would render the table board a basis]. And here [in our Mishnah], we are dealing with a cover like an earthenware vessel that is placed over the pot, where the pot is swallowed within it, and it is impossible to shake the cover unless one lifts it slightly. And the Ri explains: For example, where he insulated the pot in a basket with something that may be moved, and above the pot he filled the entire basket with something that may not be moved, such that it is impossible for him to reach the pot without moving something that may not be moved with [his] hands.

Tosafot on Shabbat 51a:2:1.hebrew: כסהו ונתגלה מותר לכסותו - נראה לר"י דה"ה דמותר לגלותו בידים ולחזור ולכסותו, כמו שמותר ליטול הקדרה ולהחזירה. והא דנקט "כסהו ונתגלה" — משום דנתגלה מבעוד יום איירי, דומיא דרישא "לא כסהו מבעוד יום", וקאמר דמותר לכסותו משתחשך. אבל אם גילהו בידים מבעוד יום כדי לכסותו משתחשך — אסור לכסותו משתחשך, דדמיא לתחלת הטמנה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 51a:2:1.english: "[If] he covered it and it became uncovered, he is permitted to cover it" - It appears to the Ri that the same law applies [such] that it is permitted to uncover it by hand and cover it again, just as it is permitted to remove the pot and return it. And that which [the Mishnah] formulated, "he covered it and it became uncovered" — [this is] because it is dealing with [a case where] it became uncovered while it was still day, parallel to the opening clause, "he did not cover it while it was still day," and it is stating that it is permitted to cover it after dark. However, if he uncovered it by hand while it was still day in order to cover it after dark, it is forbidden to cover it after dark, because it resembles initiating an insulation.

Tosafot on Shabbat 51a:6:1.hebrew: אילו היה ר' יוסי קיים היה כפוף כו' - פי' רבינו שלמה: מחמת נשיאותו — דהא ר"י היה גדול מרבי, כדמוכח בפ"ב דנדה (דף יד: ושם), דאמר ליה רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי לר' חמא בר ביסנא: "כדברי רבי אומר לך, או כדברי אבא?" אמר ליה: "כדברי רבי אמור לי". אמר ליה: "זהו שאומרים עליו דאדם גדול הוא, שמניח דברי הרב ושומע דברי התלמיד?!" ור"ת מפרש: דודאי מתחלה היה רבי תלמידו של רבי יוסי, אבל אח"כ נתחכם רבי, כדקאמ' התם: "ור' חמא סבר: רבי ריש מתיבתא, שכיחי רבנן גביה ומחדדן שמעתתיה":
Tosafot on Shabbat 51a:6:1.english: "Had Rabbi Yosei been alive, he would have been subordinate, etc." - Rabbeinu Shlomo explained: [He would have been subordinate] on account of his position as Patriarch, for Rabbi Yosei was greater than Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], as is demonstrated in the second chapter of Niddah (14b and there), where Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, said to Rabbi Ḥama bar Bisna: "Shall I tell you in accordance with the words of Rabbi, or in accordance with the words of Father?" He said to him: "Tell me in accordance with the words of Rabbi." He said to him: "Is this the one about whom they say that he is a great man, that he abandons the words of the teacher and listens to the words of the student?!" And Rabbeinu Tam explains that certainly, at first, Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] was the student of Rabbi Yosei; but afterwards, Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] became wiser [and surpassed him], as [the Gemara] says there: "And Rabbi Ḥama maintained: Rabbi is the head of the academy; the Rabbis are frequently in his presence, and his teachings are sharpened."
